title: IP addresses are numbers
description:
An IPv4 address is one 32-bit number, written as four bytes. Write:

```python
def to_number(address)            # "93.184.215.14" -> 1572394766
def to_text(number)               # and back
def same_network(a, b, prefix)    # True when the first prefix bits of the two addresses are equal
```

`same_network("192.168.1.20", "192.168.1.200", 24)` is `True`: the first 24 bits (`192.168.1`) match. That is how your computer decides whether another device is on your home network or must be reached through the router.

Shifting builds the number: `(a << 24) | (b << 16) | (c << 8) | d`. To compare the top `prefix` bits, shift both numbers right by `32 - prefix`.
